title: Realized equality of right and left finite base-change routes
statement:
theorem sixFunctorProjectionFinite_right_left_path_realized
    (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E n hn) (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
    (K : sixFunctorFiniteCategory D C E n hn Q.X)
    (L : finiteTorConstructibleCategory C.l E n hn Q.Y.obj.left) :
    letI := Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing C.l E n hn
    let I := (intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible C.l E n hn Q.Y'.obj.left).ι
    let target := sixFunctorProjectionFiniteSquareTarget S Q K L
    I.map (sixFunctorProjectionFiniteRightPath S Q K L) ≫ target.hom =
      I.map (sixFunctorProjectionFiniteLeftPath S Q K L) ≫ target.hom

source.place: Base-change paragraph, route normalization after endpoint realization

proof.text: Realize the right route independently. Expand its projection component as source comparison, realized fixed projection, and inverse target comparison, which cancels against SquareTarget. Apply the two-variable naturality of the fixed projection to move the target pullback comparisons to its source. Tensor bifunctoriality cancels the inverse coefficient comparisons in Mu against these source comparisons. The explicit exchange conjugation, after inverse realization and cancellation of the coefficient unit, becomes the fixed exchange. Naturality of the pullback tensor comparison in its first argument moves the fixed support comparison to the source. Naturality of the coefficient-equivalence unit identifies this remaining source with SquareSource. This gives SquareSource followed by the realized diamondRight, without using equality of the constructible routes. The fixed-scalar expansion into the exposed coordinate API is isolated in finiteProjectionDiamondRight_fixed_coordinates, for arbitrary derived inputs; all transport and cancellation steps are proved here. The proved private naturality lemmas in FiniteProjectionIterationRealization and the proved private exchange-transport lemma in ProjectionFiniteBaseChangeLeftPrefix supply the generic categorical APIs; the public unfinished left-prefix theorem is not used in this independent right-route calculation.
Use the existing left-route calculation to identify the realized left route with SquareSource followed by the realized diamondLeft.
Map the fixed-scalar diamond equality through the coefficient realization and precompose with SquareSource. Combine with the independently obtained right-route and left-route equations.

proof_origin.place: Base-change paragraph: independent right-route coordinate calculation, left-route calculation and fixed-scalar diamond equality.
